purpose: Test whether one already-established v0.7 multiscale EEG metric differs between healthy controls and a clinical schizophrenia cohort. This is a research group-discrimination test, not a diagnostic or biomarker claim.

source.reference: reference electrode between Fz and Cz
source.file_rule: Use exactly h01.edf..h14.edf and s01.edf..s14.edf from RepOD dataset version 1.0. Each downloaded file must match the MD5 published by RepOD before analysis.

windowing.start_index_rule: For cleaned recording length N, window k=0..11 starts at floor(k*(N-2048)/11). This deterministically spans the complete recording and is fixed before group outcomes are inspected.
windowing.finite_policy: Replace non-finite samples within a selected window with 0.0 before the unchanged operator runs.
windowing.subject_aggregation: Compute the endpoint separately in each of the 12 windows; the subject score is the median of the 12 window endpoint values. No epoch/window is treated as an independent subject.

primary_endpoint.name: median_multiscale_meanPLV_slope
primary_endpoint.per_window_metric: OLS slope of meanPhaseLocking versus scale level over nonterminal scales with node counts [19,10,5,3,2]. The terminal n=1 scale is excluded because its pair metric is structurally degenerate.
primary_endpoint.group_direction: two-sided; no direction is assumed before outcomes
primary_endpoint.primary_group_statistic: Mann-Whitney U on the 28 subject scores, exact two-sided p-value; effect size AUC = U/(14*14) reported with group direction preserved.

secondary_predeclared_endpoints: subject median of per-window kappa slope across nonterminal scales
subject median of per-window log(couplingLossQ) slope across nonterminal scales
subject median of per-window chi_dyn slope across nonterminal scales
subject median of per-window VAR-stability slope across nonterminal scales

secondary_group_discrimination.feature: primary subject score only; no feature selection and no multivariate model
secondary_group_discrimination.classifier: For each held-out subject, compute the healthy and schizophrenia medians from training subjects only and assign the held-out score to the class whose training median is closer; exact ties are assigned healthy.
secondary_group_discrimination.label_permutation_test: 10000 deterministic balanced label permutations. For permutation r, rank subjects by SHA256(validation_id|classification-permutation|r|subject); assign the 14 lowest hashes schizophrenia and the remaining 14 healthy. Recompute the full leave-one-subject-out classifier. p=(1+count(null_balanced_accuracy>=observed))/(10001).
secondary_group_discrimination.interpretation: exploratory-supporting only; not a diagnostic accuracy claim

parity_gate.comparison: At least one preregistered window from every subject must pass full Kotlin versus independent-Python parity for every scale metric and every pair metric; all 12 windows are computed by the same frozen operator implementation.

guardrails: Group labels may not be used to choose channels, windows, scale levels, preprocessing parameters, endpoint direction or metric after results are observed.
No window-level train/test split is permitted; the unit of inference is the person.
No metric may replace the primary endpoint because it separates the groups better after inspection.
A significant group difference is evidence of group discrimination in this dataset, not proof of diagnosis, causality, disease specificity, source localization, universality or a physical law.
Any algorithmic or endpoint change requires a new preregistration version and an independent dataset for confirmatory use.
